result.summary: go-logr/logr v1.4.2 is a structured-logging API (Logger/LogSink, context helpers, slog bridges); its funcr subpackage formats log lines and passes them to a caller-provided function. I read every surface file for init code, I/O, exec, network, encoded payloads, environment-dependent behaviour and text addressed to reviewers, and found none. The flagged capabilities arise only from reflection, runtime caller lookup and dynamic calls into user-supplied interfaces.

findings.title: No side effects beyond formatting and dispatch to user-supplied sinks
findings.detail: Both packages are purely in-process logging abstractions. logr defines Logger/LogSink, context helpers and slog adapters. funcr formats key/value pairs and hands the strings to a caller-supplied function. The unit has no init functions, build scripts, embedded data, encoded strings, exec, file or network I/O, or environment or credential access. The content matches the well-known upstream v1.4.2 source.

capabilities.explanation: The logr package contains no networking code. The capability is most likely inferred from its dynamic calls: user-supplied LogSink and slog.Handler implementations (slogsink.go, sloghandler.go) and the slog.Record/Value machinery, which can call String()/Error() methods of arbitrary types, including net types. Any real I/O is done by the sink or handler the application chooses.

funcr has no code that changes process or system state. The capability most likely comes from reflection used to render values (reflect.ValueOf, Field, MapRange, Interface) and from runtime.Caller/FuncForPC used for call-site attribution. It may also come from invoking user-supplied MarshalLog/String/Error methods and the caller-provided write function. These are harmless formatting operations.

funcr makes no network calls. The capability is most likely inferred conservatively from its calls through interfaces, such as fmt.Stringer, error, encoding.TextMarshaler, logr.Marshaler and the caller-supplied write func, which static analysis may resolve to network-related types. Output goes only to the function the application passes to New/NewJSON.
